correctness.rationale: The estimator is a fully specified joint-Gaussian polynomial on an isotropic quadratic. Isserlis pairing proves the exact mean operator. Conditioning on the exploratory direction and applying noncentral Gaussian fourth moments and chi-square moment identities proves the two invariant-block second-moment coefficients for every d >= k >= 1. Their nonnegative difference identifies the worst hinted direction; the scalar quadratic step factor gives the exact positive contraction interval and its unique minimizer. Above the rank-dependent correlation boundary the hinted expected iterate is nondecaying or strictly growing, so Jensen prohibits mean-square convergence at any positive step. Exact rational Wick expansion independently matched the stated mean and second moments in all 105 checked dimension/rank/correlation cases. These finite checks are supplementary, not infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The motivating paper explicitly draws exploration independently after choosing the control-variate reference; its oracle and practical constructions do not subsume an estimator with a correlated Gaussian one-probe reference. Accessible published comparisons address fixed projections, Gaussian probe covariance design, noisy independent finite differences, or differently structured fitted control variates, not this exact rank-dependent reversal and all-dimensional sharp squared-norm frontier. General dependence-induced control-variate bias is acknowledged as prior knowledge. Residual risks from uncatalogued equivalent formulas remain.
residual_risks: A preexisting equivalent Gaussian moment or in-sample baseline formula outside the inspected searchable record could subsume the proposed result.
The central model is an explicitly modified Gaussian two-probe estimator; it is not the practical independent-reference algorithm and its significance is confined to the coupling design choice.
Higher-dimensional quadratics with nonidentity Hessians, finite-difference noise and time-correlated probes are not addressed.

value.rationale: The exact rank-only correlation cutoff answers a motivated numerical design question: reusing the exploratory Gaussian data to estimate a projected reference can make the mean gradient point uphill even on the simplest strongly convex objective, and no reduction of a positive step repairs that regime. The complete conditional squared-norm formula gives sharp positive-side step calibration for all dimensions and ranks rather than only a single counterexample, with an explicit distinction from the proven original independent-reference method.
